note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe, "blinding" diffuse headache for 3 days, worse over right eye; started suddenly on waking 3 days ago and has been essentially continuous.
- Severity/timeline: Pain described as ~8/10 at worst, partially improved to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but not resolved; present throughout the day, does not wake patient at night but may be present on waking.
- Character/associated features: Photophobia and intermittent "shooting lights" / visual phenomena; feels "a bit sick" but no vomiting; occasional brief stabbing pain with rapid standing or head movement; sleeping ok.
- Triggers/relieving factors: Partial relief with ibuprofen; no clear positional/Valsalva provocation except stabbing on quick stand/head movement.
- Prior episodes: Occasional short-lived headaches in past responsive to ibuprofen; this is first prolonged severe episode.
- Recent care: Recent eye check reported as normal; pharmacy BP check ~1 year ago reported normal.
- Social/family: Lives alone; non-smoker; drinks alcohol ~once weekly; mother has severe migraines.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Surgical/other history: Not reported.
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill — name not documented; started ~1 year ago.
  - Ibuprofen as needed for headache — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol advised as adjunct by clinician — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Prescribed "a bit stronger" analgesic by clinician (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Family history: Mother with migraines (including vomiting).

Physical Examination:
- Examination performed during teleconsultation: No physical exam findings documented.
- Reported/observed status:
  - No fever reported.
  - No vomiting.
  - No reported weakness, numbness, or other focal neurological symptoms.
  - No change in smell or taste.
  - No sinus symptoms, nasal bleeding, or recent head trauma.
  - Recent eye check reported normal by patient.
- Planned in-person exam: Full neurological examination and fundoscopy (to assess for papilledema) and blood pressure check.
- If absent, write “Not recorded.”: Formal vital signs, neurological exam findings, fundoscopy, and BP not recorded during this consult.

Impression:
- Primary clinical impression: Probable migraine-type headache (possible migraine with visual phenomena/aura) based on sudden severe headache, photophobia, intermittent visual "shooting lights," family history of migraine, and partial response to analgesia.
- Additional differential diagnoses consistent with the transcript (from DDx):
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — medium likelihood: young woman on combined oral contraceptive with subacute progressive headache and visual symptoms; requires exclusion.
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — medium likelihood: persistent headache with visual disturbances in a young woman; fundoscopy needed to assess papilledema.
- No direct conflict between transcript and DDx. (DDx also considered SAH and other causes but those were ranked lower; clinician prioritized migraine and planned examination.)

Management Plan:
- Immediate/advised medications:
  - Prescribe a stronger analgesic "similar to ibuprofen but a bit stronger" — name/dose/route/frequency not documented; to be used instead of ibuprofen.
  - Paracetamol may be taken concurrently — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Advise to take prescribed medication with food.
- Diagnostics / examinations:
  - Book face-to-face appointment for full neurological examination and fundoscopy.
  - Check blood pressure at in-person visit (clinician to reassess suitability of combined OCP).
  - Further investigations (imaging, blood tests) to be arranged if abnormal exam or red flags identified (not ordered during this consult).
- Safety / escalation advice:
  - If headache worsens, becomes unbearable, changes character, or new focal neurological signs develop, go to Accident & Emergency (A&E) for urgent assessment and imaging.
  - If symptoms settle prior to appointment, the appointment may be cancelled.
- Reproductive health:
  - Continue current combined OCP for the moment; clinician noted possible need to change if regular migraines with aura are confirmed on further assessment.
- Follow-up:
  - Support team to arrange in-person appointment; clinician available for further advice before appointment if needed.

Patient Summary:
- Patient presented with a 3-day history of a sudden-onset, continuous severe headache with photophobia and intermittent visual "shooting lights." Clinician's working diagnosis is a probable migraine-type headache, but secondary causes (notably CVST or IIH) must be excluded due to oral contraceptive use and persistence of symptoms. Plan is an in-person neurological exam and fundoscopy, prescription of a stronger analgesic plus paracetamol (take with food), and instruction to seek emergency care if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed stronger analgesic (instead of ibuprofen) and you may take paracetamol as advised — take medications with food.
- Book and attend the in-person appointment for neurological exam and fundoscopy; BP will be checked and OCP reviewed if needed.
- Go to A&E urgently if headache becomes much worse, changes, or new neurological signs occur.

Next Steps:
- Support team to schedule face-to-face appointment for neurological examination and fundoscopy.
- At that visit: measure blood pressure, perform full neuro exam, and consider urgent neuroimaging or specialist referral if exam is abnormal or red flags present.
- Reassess need to continue or change combined oral contraceptive if migraine with aura or other concerning findings are confirmed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature) not recorded.
  - Formal neurological exam findings and fundoscopy results not recorded.
  - Exact names, doses, routes, and frequencies of prescribed analgesic and paracetamol not documented.
  - No imaging or laboratory results available.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted; DDx considerations (migraine, CVST, IIH, SAH) align with transcript and clinician plan to examine and exclude secondary causes.
- Transcript quality:
  - Mostly clear; several brief inaudible/ellipsed moments early in the recording (patient identification and some small details), but overall history and plan are adequately documented.
